title: Axis rises above 200% when the shown values are mostly high
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in one location (workplace) with the data below.
  3. You use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor).
  4. A technician whose only clocked work this month is billed far above the time clocked exists: one invoiced work order today with one labor line of 1.00 hour assigned to that technician, who clocked exactly 0.25 hours on it (1.00 / 0.25 x 100 = 400%).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site use Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 unless a later line says otherwise.
  • For 4: use a technician with no other clocked time this month: create a new technician you can sign in as: profile icon > Settings > Staff > New Staff Member: a name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Tech), an Email you can open, Role Technician, a Department, Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close; accept the invitation email and set a password. Then Customers > New Customer > Name > Save (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer); Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = that technician, Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; then the Service Advisor is filled in with your name (Admin ShopView); to use another advisor change Service Advisor in the work order's left panel; clock time as that technician in a private window; open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start; when done click Stop > Clock Out; make the clocked time exactly 0.25 hours (15 minutes), as Admin: the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice).
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. On the Technician Efficiency tile, click View details.
  3. In the Technician filter, untick everyone except the seeded technician.
  4. Hover the technician's point and read its value.
  5. Read the top label of the left-hand axis.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Only one point is plotted and it reads about 400% (every shown value is above 200%, so the middle value is above 200%).
  • The axis is not capped at 200%: it rises to fit the value, with a top label at or above 400%, and the point is drawn in full, not clipped.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 9. Context note on the axis (Story 9). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, screenshots of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28) board 06_TechEff_After, used for on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.”
  • Context note (Story 9, the axis): “the axis fits the data. It only pins to 200% when a single outlier would otherwise flatten the rest of the chart; when the data as a whole is genuinely high, the axis scales up to fit it. This behavior applies wherever the chart appears — inside an expanded tile and embedded on a report page (Story 11).”
